report.source_text: From the second day of pulse steroid therapy, an increase in the eGFR, a decrease in the troponin I and NT-proBNP levels, and a reduction in the frequency of sinus pauses were observed. In addition, AF disappeared completely and never recurred.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old woman with squamous cell lung carcinoma treated with pembrolizumab monotherapy developed high fever, worsening kidney function, and symptomatic sinus node dysfunction with pauses and atrial fibrillation. Cardiac biomarkers troponin I and NT-proBNP were elevated on admission, indicating myocardial injury. Endomyocardial biopsy performed on day 4 after steroid initiation revealed infiltration of CD3-positive lymphocytes and CD163-positive macrophages, PD-L1 positivity, and tenascin-C expression consistent with myocarditis. Treatment with pulse steroids led to improvement in kidney function, reduction in cardiac biomarkers, resolution of atrial fibrillation, and decreased sinus pauses, confirming the diagnosis of immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis as the cause of sinus node damage.
